title: Menachem Talmia
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: At the end of Yerushalmi Sanhedrin, chapter 2, Rabbi Yochanan told Rabbi Yudan Nesia, “Send for Menachem Talmia.” (It appears that Menachem Talmish was a great man, a sage and a scribe; Rabbi Yudan Nesia had asked Rabbi Yochanan about some secret matter, and he answered that he should send for Menachem.) As it is written, “The teaching of kindness is on her tongue.” In Kohelet Rabbah, chapter 5, on “When they increase,” Rabbi Chananiah and Rabbi Yonatan asked Menachem Talmia. Rabbi Berechyah, in Rabbi Yosi bar Ch.’s name, says instead that Menachem Talmia asked them, etc.[^1]

notes.text: The parenthesis is Hyman’s conjecture, introduced by “it appears.” Talmish (טלמיש) there differs from Talmia elsewhere. The repeated ר״י initials refer to the two preceding names; the patronymic בר״ח remains “bar Ch.” The final reports reverse who asked whom. The locators give the end of Sanhedrin chapter 2 and Kohelet Rabbah chapter 5; the verse opening ברבות is translated without a verse number.
